points.title: The trolls' warning
points.kid: The trolls say the head can be persuaded, but the heart is harder. What do you think that means?
points.parent: The whole movie is set up in this one line of folk wisdom. Notice what the grown-ups do with the warning: they erase Anna's memory and hide Elsa away — they treat a HEART problem with a HEAD solution. Watch how that works out.

options.reply: That's what we might hope — but watch again. The gates close, the staff is reduced, the gloves go on...

options.text: Hide them — gloves, closed gates, secrets
options.reply: YES. They choose hiding over practicing. It comes from love AND fear at once — and it becomes the armor Elsa carries for the whole movie.
No — they keep her home. But home becomes a kind of hiding place.

quiz.question: What do the parents decide to do about Elsa's powers?

points.title: Love Is an Open Door
points.kid: Anna wants to marry Hans the day she met him! What do you think about that?
points.parent: The movie deliberately sets up the fairy-tale shortcut so it can question it later. A kid-sized way in: how long does it take to really know a friend? Anna has been lonely behind closed gates for years — the loneliness, not silliness, is what makes the shortcut tempting.

options.text: Because Hans is definitely her true love
options.reply: The movie has a BIG surprise about that. Keep watching...

options.text: Because she's been lonely for so long
options.reply: YES. Years of closed doors made an open door feel like everything. Loneliness can make us decide too fast.

options.text: Because the trolls told her to
options.reply: The trolls aren't here — this one is all Anna.

quiz.question: Why does Anna say yes so fast?

points.title: Let It Go
points.kid: Elsa finally uses her powers and builds something beautiful. Is she free now, or alone — or both?
points.parent: The trick of this scene: it FEELS like pure victory, and it's half of one. Elsa drops the armor of hiding — real progress — but swaps it for the armor of distance (a palace with no door handles, on a mountain, alone). Same tension as Moana's ocean and Rumi's stage: the truth is out, but connection still missing.

options.reply: It IS beautiful. But count the people in it...
YES. She traded hiding-among-people for shining-alone. Free AND lonely can be true at the same time.

quiz.question: Elsa builds an amazing ice palace. What's missing from it?

points.title: An act of true love
points.kid: Only an act of true love can thaw a frozen heart. What counts as an act of true love?
points.parent: Everyone in the movie — and most of us watching — assumes it means a kiss someone GIVES you. The ending flips it: the act of true love is one Anna DOES. Pause here and collect guesses; the wrong guesses are the fun part.
